note: Style sheets describe techniques only. They never name or reproduce the notes, themes or progressions of an existing piece.

sheets.name: Bittersweet orchestral
sheets.summary: Slow, bittersweet film-cue writing: piano and massed strings over a rocking compound pulse, opening quietly on warm colour chords, developing without literal repeats to one earned arrival, more often still and bright than loud, and a late dark turn.
traits: slow compound pulse: 12/8 at 68-75 BPM, felt as four rocking beats
minor tonal centre (for example C-sharp minor) with planned key changes
opens on a warm two-chord oscillation of major-seventh and ninth chords
piano states the idea alone; strings take it over and widen it
strings at scale: the weight of a 40+ player orchestra, in octaves and divided parts
quiet, thin start; one layer added at a time
peaks and lulls planned in advance, each peak higher than the last
constant development: every restatement varied, almost no exact repetition
pedal tones held under shifting harmony
phrase endings left unresolved or half-resolved to pull the line onward
a pause or sudden thinning just before the arrival

the arrival late in the piece is earned by steady momentum, then released: usually a gentle, serene opening-out (the pulse stops, chords are held, the theme sings high and slow); a full-orchestra wall only when the prompt asks for something vast or violent
late dark turn with late-Romantic, Russian-style chromatic chords
short afterglow that dissolves instead of closing firmly

harmonicLanguage: borrowed chords from the parallel mode
key changes by step or third
late chromatic chords: augmented sixth, diminished seventh, lowered second and sixth degrees
defaults.soundWorld: Soft-attack piano and a large, warm string section in a spacious hall; woodwind and horn as quiet colour, harp and timpani for swells, cymbal and bass drum only for a rare wall-of-sound climax.

avoid: copying or paraphrasing the notes of any existing piece
repeating a phrase exactly more than twice
a full tonic close before the final section
loud dynamics or full scoring in the first third
a steady drum-kit or electronic beat
fast chord changes in quiet passages
a bright ending that resolves everything
every instrument doubling all the time
a climax that is only louder: more noise without a change of colour, register or motion

sheets.name: Beat-driven
sheets.summary: Loop-based electronic writing on a steady 4/4 pulse: kick and sub bass lock the groove, syncopated hats push it forward, short motif cells repeat and mutate, and energy is shaped by filter builds, drops and sidechain pump.
traits: steady 4/4 kick pulse, no tempo change
sine sub bass on chord roots, locked to the kick
syncopated, off-beat hi-hats
short motif cells of two to four notes, looped
variation by adding, muting and filtering layers, not by new melody
filter-sweep builds over four or eight bars
drop: kick and bass return together after a break
sidechain pump: pad and bass duck on every kick
eight-bar blocks grouped into sixteen-bar sections
breakdown that strips back to pad and motif
noise risers and falls at section joins
looped two- to four-chord harmony
a chorus that adds what the verse held back: another instrument on the hook, keys or strings filling the chords, a step up in level

harmonicLanguage: modal harmony with few functional cadences
defaults.soundWorld: Dry, punchy production: 808 kick or drum kit, sine sub, tight hats, pluck synth and wide pad, filtered noise for transitions. Electric piano, a synth lead on the hook, supersaw chords, a moving synth bass, bell sparkles and synth-brass stabs are the colours of the style, used above all to make a chorus bigger than a verse. No orchestral instruments.

avoid: rubato, pauses or tempo changes inside a section
long through-composed melodies
dense orchestral doubling
anything sounding below the sub bass
frequent key changes
bass notes that do not land with the kick pattern

sheets.name: Playful
sheets.summary: Light, bright and quick on its feet: pizzicato strings and staccato woodwinds trade bouncing figures in major and Lydian colours, with sudden stops, quick register jumps and short, tidy phrases.
traits: bright modes: major, Lydian, Mixolydian
pizzicato strings as the rhythmic bed
staccato articulation, short notes with air between them
woodwinds carry the tune: flute, oboe and clarinet in dialogue
bouncing rhythms: dotted figures, off-beat accents, upbeat starts
sudden stops and one-beat silences
quick register jumps and octave displacement
short question-and-answer phrases of two or four bars
call and response between instruments
bell-like touches from glockenspiel, celesta and harp
grace notes and quick scale runs
surprise dynamics: sudden soft, sudden accent
clear cadences, tossed off lightly

harmonicLanguage: secondary dominants as a passing wink
sudden shifts up a step or a third
raised fourth degree for Lydian brightness
defaults.soundWorld: Small, dry chamber-orchestra sound, close and nimble: plucked strings, chattering woodwinds and bell-like percussion, with nothing sustained for long.

avoid: long sustained pads or pedal points
heavy low-register doubling
slow chord changes
brooding minor passages or unresolved endings
full tutti for more than a bar or two
legato lines longer than one phrase
sub bass and heavy kick
